key_insight: This paper introduces FlatSounds, a benchmark that tests whether video-to-audio models understand physical cause-and-effect, not just whether their outputs sound realistic. It shows that perceptual quality alone is not enough to judge true physical reasoning in generative V2A systems.
problem_solved: Current video-to-audio evaluations focus on how natural or believable the audio sounds, but they do not check whether models respond correctly to controlled changes in physical conditions. This paper addresses the lack of a benchmark for testing physical correctness under single-factor interventions.
method: Introduces FlatSounds, a benchmark designed to audit physical reasoning in video-to-audio generation models.
Uses controlled counterfactual pairs where exactly one physical variable is changed to isolate causal effects.
Includes single-video pattern tests to probe whether models infer consistent physical audio patterns from one clip.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more rigorous way to evaluate V2A models beyond surface-level realism. It helps identify models that sound convincing but fail at physically grounded reasoning, which is important for robust multimodal generation.
visual_elements: Side-by-side counterfactual video pairs showing one changed physical factor

paper_authors: Tingle Li, Siddharth Gururani, Kevin J. Shih, Gantavya Bhatt, Sang-gil Lee
